claims.text: The intervention changes Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2 by replacing 2 at.% P with 2 at.% B.
Adding 2 at.% B will enhance the alloy's glass-forming ability.
Adding 2 at.% B will enhance the alloy's thermal stability during reheating.
B substitution will increase atomic-size mismatch in the liquid and glass.
B substitution will produce stronger P–B and metal–B covalent bonding in the liquid and glass.
B addition increases the alloy's mixing enthalpy.
B addition reduces atomic mobility.
Reduced atomic mobility raises the activation barrier for nucleation and growth of crystalline phases.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2 will form fully amorphous ribbons at cooling rates of at least 1×10^4 K/s.
The baseline Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy exhibits only limited or partial amorphous retention even at cooling rates of at least 1×10^6 K/s.
The baseline alloy has a supercooled liquid region ΔTx of approximately 20 K.
B substitution will increase ΔTx by approximately 20 K relative to the baseline alloy.
The baseline alloy has a crystallization onset temperature Tx of approximately 500 K.
B substitution will increase Tx by approximately 30 K relative to the baseline alloy.
The B-modified alloy will remain amorphous without premature crystallization when reheated at 20 K/min to 550 K.
The baseline alloy crystallizes rapidly on reheating.
Below a cooling rate of 1×10^4 K/s, the B-modified alloy is expected to be partially amorphous or non-glassy.
Enhanced stability may not persist at reheating rates above 50 K/min.
Enhanced stability may not persist when the peak reheating temperature exceeds 550 K.
B is known to improve glass-forming ability in Ni–P systems.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts partial or no glass below 1×10^4 K/s, but the falsification rule treats failure to obtain a fully amorphous structure at cooling rates ≤1×10^4 K/s as falsifying. Thus an expected result at 1×10^3 K/s would incorrectly trigger falsification.
